title: Human Health and Diseases
subject: Biology
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET / NEET • Quick Revision

nodes.title: Concept of Health & Innate vs Acquired Immunity
points: Health (WHO): State of complete physical, mental, and social well-being, not merely the absence of disease or infirmity.

Innate Immunity (Non-specific, inborn defense): 1) Physical (Skin stratum corneum, mucus coating of tracts); 2) Physiological (Stomach HCl, lysozyme in saliva/tears); 3) Cellular (PMNL neutrophils, monocytes, macrophages, Natural Killer NK cells); 4) Cytokine barriers (Interferons secreted by virus-infected cells protect healthy cells).
Acquired Immunity (Specific, with memory):
- Active Immunity: Developed by host's own immune system upon antigen exposure (slow, long-lasting memory); Natural (clinical infection) or Artificial (vaccines).

- Passive Immunity: Ready-made antibodies received from outside (immediate, no memory); Natural (maternal IgG across placenta, secretory IgA in colostrum) or Artificial (anti-tetanus serum ATS, anti-snake venom).

formulas.label: Innate immunity 4-barrier defense
formulas.expr: Physical (Skin/Mucus) + Physiological (HCl/Lysozyme) + Cellular (PMNL/Macrophages) + Cytokine (Interferons)

formulas.label: Active vs Passive immunity
formulas.expr: Active: Host produces antibodies (Memory formed, slow) | Passive: Ready-made antibodies injected (No memory, rapid)

nodes.title: Immune Cells & Antibody Structure (H₂L₂)
points: Lymphocytes: 1) T-Cells (mature in Thymus): Mediate Cell-Mediated Immunity (CMI); responsible for graft rejection in organ transplants! Subsets: Helper T (CD4⁺, activate B-cells), Cytotoxic T (CD8⁺, release perforins to lyse infected cells), Suppressor T, Memory T; 2) B-Cells (mature in Bone marrow): Mediate Humoral / Antibody-Mediated Immunity (AMI); differentiate into Plasma cells (secrete ~2000 antibodies/sec) and Memory B-cells.
Antibody Structure: Y-shaped glycoprotein represented as H₂L₂ (2 identical Heavy chains + 2 identical Light chains held by disulfide −S−S− bonds).
Variable region (Fab): Contains Antigen-binding site (Paratope) complementary to antigen Epitope. Constant region (Fc): Determines immunoglobulin class.

Immunoglobulin classes (GAMED): IgG (most abundant 80%, only one crossing placenta), IgA (secretory dimer in colostrum/saliva), IgM (largest pentamer, primary response), IgE (allergies, mast cell histamine release), IgD (B-cell receptor).

formulas.label: Antibody chain stoichiometry
formulas.expr: H₂L₂ (2 Heavy chains ~50 kDa + 2 Light chains ~25 kDa held by disulfide −S−S− bonds)

formulas.label: Immunoglobulins classes summary (GAMED)
formulas.expr: IgG (crosses placenta) | IgA (secretory dimer in colostrum) | IgM (pentamer, first responder) | IgE (allergy & histamine) | IgD

formulas.label: Paratope-Epitope interaction
formulas.expr: Paratope (antigen-binding site on Fab arm of antibody) binds Epitope (antigenic determinant on antigen)

nodes.title: Bacterial & Viral Diseases: Typhoid, Pneumonia, Common Cold
points: 1. Typhoid: Pathogen: Salmonella typhi (Gram-negative bacillus); transmitted through contaminated food and water. Enters small intestine, causing mucosal ulceration. Symptoms: Sustained high fever (39-40 °C), headache, stomach pain, constipation, loss of appetite, pea-soup stools. Diagnosis: Widal Test. Famous carrier: Mary Mallon (Typhoid Mary).

2. Pneumonia: Pathogens: Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae. Infects alveoli of lungs; alveoli become fluid-filled impairing gas exchange. Symptoms: Fever, chills, cough with rusty sputum, headache; lips and nails turn gray to bluish in severe cases. Transmitted by aerosol droplets.
3. Common Cold: Pathogen: Rhinoviruses. Infects nasal and respiratory mucosa, but NEVER infects the lungs! Symptoms: Nasal congestion, discharge, sore throat, cough, hoarseness lasting 3-7 days.

formulas.label: Typhoid pathogen & diagnosis
formulas.expr: Pathogen: Salmonella typhi | Diagnostic test: Widal test | Target: Small intestine (ulceration)

formulas.label: Pneumonia vs Common Cold target
formulas.expr: Pneumonia: Alveoli of lungs (fluid accumulation) | Common Cold: Upper respiratory tract (lungs NOT infected)

nodes.title: Protozoan Diseases: Malaria & Amoebiasis
points: 1. Malaria: Pathogen: Plasmodium (P. vivax, P. malariae, P. falciparum; P. falciparum causes malignant tertian / cerebral malaria, fatal). Vector: Female Anopheles mosquito.

Digenetic life cycle of Plasmodium: 1) Mosquito bite injects motile Sporozoites into human blood → enter Liver cells (hepatic schizogony) → burst liver cells releasing merozoites into RBCs; 2) In RBCs (erythrocytic schizogony), trophozoite feeds and ruptures RBCs releasing Hemozoin toxin (triggers recurring chills and high fever every 48-72 hours!); 3) Gametocytes develop in RBCs; 4) Female Anopheles ingests gametocytes; fertilization occurs in mosquito gut; sporozoites migrate to salivary glands.

2. Amoebiasis (Amoebic Dysentery): Pathogen: Entamoeba histolytica (protozoan in large intestine). Mechanical vector: Housefly (Musca domestica). Symptoms: Constipation, abdominal pain, stools with excess mucus and blood clots.

formulas.label: Malaria life cycle stages
formulas.expr: Sporozoites (infective to man) → Liver cells → RBCs (rupture + Hemozoin release = Chills & Fever) → Gametocytes (infective to mosquito)

formulas.label: Hemozoin toxin role
formulas.expr: Rupture of erythrocytic schizonts releases Hemozoin pigment → Triggers recurring high fever with chills

formulas.label: Amoebiasis pathogen & vector
formulas.expr: Entamoeba histolytica (large intestine parasite) | Mechanical vector: Housefly (Musca domestica)

nodes.title: Helminthic & Fungal Diseases: Ascariasis, Filariasis & Ringworm
points: 1. Ascariasis: Pathogen: Ascaris lumbricoides (intestinal giant roundworm). Transmitted by fecal-oral contamination of water, vegetables, fruits with embryonated eggs. Symptoms: Internal bleeding, muscular pain, fever, anemia, intestinal blockage.

2. Filariasis / Elephantiasis: Pathogen: Filarial worms Wuchereria bancrofti and Wuchereria malayi. Vector: Female Culex mosquito. Parasites lodge in lymphatic vessels of lower limbs and genital organs causing chronic inflammation, extreme swelling of legs and scrotum.

3. Ringworm (Dermatophytosis): Fungi belonging to genera Microsporum, Trichophyton, and Epidermophyton. Symptoms: Dry, scaly, intensely itchy circular lesions on skin, scalp, groin, nails. Heat and moisture help them grow. Transmitted via towels, clothes, combs.

formulas.label: Helminthic diseases vectors & agents
formulas.expr: Filariasis: Wuchereria bancrofti (Culex mosquito vector, lymphatic blockage) | Ascariasis: Ascaris (fecal-oral)

formulas.label: Ringworm fungal genera triad
formulas.expr: Microsporum, Trichophyton, Epidermophyton (dermatophytes feeding on skin keratin)

nodes.title: AIDS & HIV Replication Life Cycle
points: AIDS: Caused by Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), an enveloped Retrovirus containing 2 identical single-stranded RNA molecules and Reverse Transcriptase, surrounded by p24 capsid and gp120 glycoprotein spikes.
Transmission: Sexual contact, contaminated blood transfusion, shared needles, infected mother to child across placenta.

HIV Life Cycle: 1) HIV gp120 binds CD4 receptors on Helper T-cells (T_H) and Macrophages; 2) Viral RNA converted to viral DNA by Reverse Transcriptase; 3) Integrase incorporates viral DNA into host genome; 4) Macrophages act as 'HIV factory'; 5) HIV attacks Helper T-cells, destroying them until CD4⁺ count drops below 200 cells/mm³, causing immunodeficiency and fatal opportunistic infections (Mycobacterium, Toxoplasma, Cytomegalovirus).
Diagnosis & Therapy: Screening test: ELISA; Confirmatory test: Western Blot. Treatment: Antiretroviral drugs (HAART) like AZT (Zidovudine) prolong life.

formulas.label: HIV replication enzyme sequence
formulas.expr: Viral ssRNA → (Reverse Transcriptase) → cDNA → (Integrase) → Host Genome Integration → mRNA/Proteins

formulas.label: Diagnostic tests for HIV
formulas.expr: Screening test: ELISA | Confirmatory test: Western Blot (detects specific viral antibodies)

formulas.label: Clinical AIDS threshold
formulas.expr: T_H (CD4⁺) count drops below 200 cells/mm³ (opportunistic infections emerge)

nodes.title: Cancer: Types, Carcinogens & Detection/Therapy
points: Cancer: Uncontrolled, abnormal mitotic proliferation of cells with loss of contact inhibition (normal cells inhibit division upon contact with neighbors).

Tumor types: Benign (localized, non-invasive) vs Malignant (invasive, destructive). Metastasis: Malignant cells detach and travel via bloodstream to establish secondary tumors at distant sites (hallmark of malignancy).
Cancer types: Carcinoma (epithelial tissue cancer: skin, breast, lung; 85%); Sarcoma (connective tissue/bone/muscle cancer); Leukemia (blood cancer, abnormal WBCs); Lymphoma (lymphatic cancer).
Carcinogens: Physical (ionizing X-rays, UV radiation); Chemical (tobacco smoke, coal tar); Biological (Oncogenic viruses, cellular proto-oncogenes activated to oncogenes).

Detection & Therapy: Biopsy, CT scan, MRI, monoclonal antibodies. Treatment: Surgery, Radiotherapy, Chemotherapy (Vincristine, Vinblastine from Catharanthus roseus), Immunotherapy (α-interferon biological response modifiers).

formulas.label: Cancer types classification key
formulas.expr: Carcinoma = Epithelial tissues | Sarcoma = Mesodermal / Connective tissues | Leukemia = Blood / Bone marrow

formulas.label: Metastasis definition
formulas.expr: Detachment and dissemination of malignant cells to distant sites establishing secondary tumors

formulas.label: Chemotherapeutic plant alkaloids
formulas.expr: Vinblastine and Vincristine (derived from Madagascar periwinkle Catharanthus roseus)

nodes.title: Drug and Alcohol Abuse: Opioids, Cannabinoids & Hallucinogens
points: 1. Opioids: Bind specific opioid receptors in CNS and GI tract. Morphine (extracted from latex of unripe seed pods of Papaver somniferum / Opium poppy; effective analgesic/sedative). Heroin (Smack / Diacetylmorphine, synthesized by acetylation of morphine; depressant that slows body functions).
2. Cannabinoids: Interact with cannabinoid receptors in brain. Derived from inflorescences of Cannabis sativa. Products: Marijuana, Hashish, Charas, Ganja. Affect cardiovascular system.
3. Hallucinogens: Alter perceptions, thoughts, feelings. Obtained from Atropa belladonna, Datura, and fungus Claviceps purpurea (LSD / Lysergic acid diethylamide).
4. Cocaine (Coke / Crack): Extracted from coca plant Erythroxylum coca. Inhibits reuptake of neurotransmitter Dopamine in CNS; produces euphoria and stimulation; overdose causes hallucinations.

formulas.label: Heroin chemical identity
formulas.expr: Diacetylmorphine = Morphine + Acetic anhydride (depressant, slows down body functions)

formulas.label: Drug categories and plant sources
formulas.expr: Opioids: Papaver somniferum | Cannabinoids: Cannabis sativa | Cocaine: Erythroxylum coca | LSD: Claviceps purpurea

formulas.label: Cocaine action mechanism
formulas.expr: Blocks reuptake of neurotransmitter Dopamine in CNS synapses → Euphoria & hallucinations

nodes.title: High-Weightage Board Questions & Distinctions
points: Board Q1: Describe the structure of an antibody molecule with a neat labelled diagram (H₂L₂, variable/constant regions, disulfide bonds).
Board Q2: Explain the life cycle of Plasmodium in human body and mosquito with a schematic diagram.
Board Q3: Explain the structure of HIV and why it is called a retrovirus. Describe the mechanism of infection.
Board Distinguish 1: Innate immunity vs Acquired immunity (non-specific, inborn vs pathogen-specific, memory-based).
Board Distinguish 2: Active immunity vs Passive immunity (slow, long-lasting memory vs immediate, short-lived without memory).
Board Distinguish 3: Benign tumor vs Malignant tumor.

formulas.label: Innate vs Acquired immunity distinction
formulas.expr: Innate: Non-specific, present from birth, no memory | Acquired: Pathogen-specific, develops with age, has memory

formulas.label: Active vs Passive immunity contrast
formulas.expr: Active: Slow, creates memory, long-lasting | Passive: Immediate, no memory, temporary

nodes.title: MHT-CET & NEET High-Speed Shortcuts & Traps
points: TRAP 1: Graft rejection in organ transplantation: Mediated by Cell-Mediated Immunity (CMI) via T-lymphocytes. Tissue matching and blood group matching are essential; immunosuppressants (Cyclosporin A) required for life.
TRAP 2: Only antibody that crosses the placenta: IgG (smallest and most abundant ~80%). Colostrum contains secretory IgA (dimer). Allergy antibody = IgE.
TRAP 3: Common cold vs Pneumonia: Common cold affects UPPER respiratory tract (nose, throat), NEVER the lungs. Pneumonia affects ALVEOLI of lungs.
TRAP 4: Typhoid Mary: Mary Mallon was an asymptomatic chronic carrier of Salmonella typhi who spread typhoid to dozens of people through food she cooked.
TRAP 5: Morphine vs Heroin: Heroin is DIACETYLMORPHINE (formed by acetylation of morphine). Both are depressants. Cocaine is a STIMULANT that inhibits dopamine reuptake.

formulas.label: Organ transplant graft rejection
formulas.expr: Mediated by T-lymphocytes (Cell-Mediated Immunity CMI)

formulas.label: Immunoglobulin roles memory trick
formulas.expr: IgG = Crosses placenta | IgA = Colostrum / Secretions | IgM = Massive pentamer | IgE = Allergy

formulas.label: Common cold pathogen trap
formulas.expr: Rhinovirus causes Common Cold (affects nose & throat, NOT lungs)
